findings.classification: material design requirement; current implementation not reviewed
findings.problem: A fresh SnapshotFileHashes owner does not by itself prevent an old semantic _history_cache hit from returning before validate_files/historical_checker. Standalone history APIs accept caller-provided cache; historical Checkers retain _history_stack and therefore do not reset that semantic cache on a repeated run. If such a cache outlives its active IO owner, a new invocation can read/hash only the envelope, return the old semantic result, register no snapshot members, and end-audit an empty union after a historical payload changed.
required_resolution_options: Tie semantic cache entries or cache-container trust to the active invocation owner/generation; invalidate or revalidate entries from another/inactive owner.

Alternatively record complete dependency binding/signature union alongside each semantic result and freshly register/verify that union plus expected hashes/membership on every semantic cache hit. Envelope read_ref hash alone is insufficient.
tests_needed: Validate context/attempt with caller-retained cache, end scope, mutate referenced snapshot, call again with same semantic cache: must block.
Repeated run on retained historical Checker must not revive old semantic trust.
Nested same-owner semantic hits remain fast but their complete dependent file union remains audited.

findings.priority: P1 if implemented with raw path stat; otherwise verification requirement
findings.problem: The listed dev/ino/size/mtime_ns/ctime_ns tuple is safe only if supplied through existing platform-aware _regular. On Windows path ctime can be creation time; _regular deliberately opens a no-follow descriptor and obtains the native metadata-change clock. A new cache built from Path.stat/lstat can trust same-size edited bytes after mtime restoration.
findings.required_resolution: Use existing _regular (or exactly equivalent descriptor-safe provider) for initial, reuse and final audit signatures. Do not substitute raw lstat on Windows.
tests_needed: Existing Windows restored-mtime same-size replacement/edit fixture must cover shared cache hit and scope final audit.
POSIX parent-symlink/ancestor escape, replacement inode, missing file and first-read mutation remain blocked.

accepted_design_properties: Dedicated SHA/signature owner separate from _history_cache and _history_stack is the right reuse boundary. No validation-result caching or source/evidence semantic shortcuts are needed for the8GB legacy repeated-read problem.
Each caller still compares its own expected hash, exact snapshot_root/logical membership and safe physical path even when a physical digest is reused.
Explicit owner transfer into historical and progress children addresses separate importlib module aliases more reliably than ambient ContextVar state alone.
Fresh top-level run, standalone history scope and inactive-owner invalidation prevent persistent trust.
Every scope exit audits child-used paths; root final exit must audit union after projections and nested semantic operations, including exception paths.
Streaming first-read stable hash avoids large whole-buffer allocation without excluding a single failed history member.

implementation_acceptance_requirements.requirement: ContextVar instances in different module aliases are distinct. Explicitly transferred owner must be the same object and all nested depths must share one lifetime. Do not use isinstance against a duplicate module class to silently drop sharing. Inactive retained owner must never be reactivated; create a fresh owner. Reset token/deactivate/clear must execute even when final audit raises.

Audit even if body raises or nested failure is caught. A root union audit failure must block/raise before the caller can observe a passed report. Preserve useful original error if audit also fails. Do not let finally cleanup clear entries before audit or let mutation failure disappear on a later retry within same invocation.

Existing ordinary file_hash/json/section caches and their mutation guards remain intact. Shared historical digest delegation must still put child-only paths in the root union or otherwise guarantee root end audit. Every expected hash comparison stays outside digest memoization.

Reusing the same physical digest for different logical refs never reuses a prior membership verdict. Snapshot-root/logical equality, safe logical path and no-linked physical path checks must execute for each reference. File additions outside declared inventory should retain whichever existing directory/membership contract currently applies; do not claim a stronger check unless implemented.

Store only signatures+digests and bounded metadata, not payload buffers. No cross-CLI disk cache. Repeated nested full-union stat audits may still be expensive; measure later, without trading away final union audit.

planned_review_after_freeze: Review actual owner scope entry/exit and all standalone history entrypoints.
Verify same-owner vs stale-owner semantic cache hits, cross-alias explicit owner attachment, repeated top-level calls and error exits.
Verify no current expected-hash/membership checks move behind a successful cached result.
Inspect focused mutation/Windows/lifetime tests and actual results; design alone is not code or runtime acceptance.
current_limits: Worker implementation is concurrently owned and unfrozen. These are design findings against documented contract and existing baseline cache behavior; no claim is made about whether in-flight code has already resolved them.
